findings.title: After logout, browser Back shows the previous user's settings page from the HTTP cache (no Cache-Control on API responses)
findings.steps: 1) Log in. 2) Type /settings?tab=account in the address bar (a full page load). 3) Type /chat in the address bar. 4) Account menu > Log out, which lands on /login. 5) Press the browser Back button.
findings.expected: The session is gone, so the page should go to /login and show no account data.
findings.actual: /settings shows the previous user's email, name and registration date, with 0 cookies in the jar. CDP shows GET /api/me came back as 200 from the disk cache (fromDiskCache=true), so AuthGate thinks the user is still logged in. The Account and General tabs make no other API calls, so the page stays up. On /media the 401 from /api/media sends the user to /login. Backend responses for /api/me, /api/conversations and /api/me/export have no Cache-Control header.
findings.evidence: /tmp/pwrun/ft_auth/ui6_cache.mjs -> ui6.out ('start=/settings?tab=account: path=/settings email-visible=true ... cookies=0', 'afterBack 200 /me disk=true'); screenshots /tmp/pwrun/ft_auth/u6__settings_tab_account.png and /tmp/pwrun/ft_auth/u1_after_logout.png; api_extra.out 'GET /me Cache-Control: None'
findings.suspected_location: backend/app/main.py (no middleware adds Cache-Control: no-store to /api responses); frontend/src/lib/me.ts:31 fetchMe uses the default fetch cache mode. Fix: add Cache-Control: no-store (or private, no-cache) on authenticated responses, and/or pass cache: 'no-store' in request()/fetchMe.

findings.title: Logout does not invalidate the session token on the server (JWT valid for 7 more days)
findings.steps: 1) POST /api/auth/register and copy the omniai_session cookie value. 2) POST /api/auth/logout (returns 204, cookie deleted). 3) GET /api/auth/me with the copied cookie value.
findings.expected: 401: a token should stop working once the user logs out.
findings.actual: 200: the old token works until it expires (session_days=7). Only 'Log out of all devices' and password change bump token_version. The cookie is httpOnly, so this needs a stolen token, but logout does not end the session.
findings.evidence: /tmp/pwrun/ft_auth/api_auth.py -> api_auth.out: 'FAIL old token after plain logout is rejected server-side :: reuse status=200'
findings.suspected_location: backend/app/routers/auth.py:81 logout() only calls response.delete_cookie. Possible fix: a per-token jti denylist, or bump token_version on logout (that would also log out other devices).

reports.harness_notes:
All scripts and outputs are in /tmp/pwrun/ft_auth/ (api_auth.py/.out, api_extra.py/.out, race.py, ui1_login.mjs to ui10_export_stale.mjs with their .out files, plus the screenshots). No repo files were edited and no shared services were touched. All accounts created are auth-*@example.com.

Things that are not product bugs:
1) api_auth.out marks 'PATCH /me mass-assignment' as FAIL. That is a mistake in my test (I compared against a mixed-case email). The stored email and id did not change.
2) The JWT check accepts a token with no 'exp' claim. Only someone holding SECRET_KEY can mint one, so I am not reporting it.
3) The cookie has no Secure flag because the local config uses cookie_secure=false. docker-compose.prod.yml sets COOKIE_SECURE=true; I could not test that.
4) Server detail messages (409/401/429/400) are Uzbek-only in EN/RU. This is already a roadmap item, so I did not count it. Only the frontend's own hard-coded strings are reported.
5) Playwright's route.fulfill skips CORS, so I could not show the 'no CORS header on 500' case with a fake response. I reproduced it with a real two-browser race instead (ui8).
6) In ui4 scenario A (Back after logout onto /chat), no data showed because /chat was not served from cache. The cache leak shows up when the previous page was /settings (ui5/ui6).

Not tested: ALLOW_REGISTRATION=false, the legacy local@omniai.dev takeover, and X-Forwarded-For handling. These need config or DB changes on shared infrastructure.

From code review only, not observed: the login limiter keeps its counts in memory per process, and the prod Dockerfile runs 2 workers, so the real limit may be up to 2x5 attempts. Registration has no rate limit, and each scrypt hash uses about 32 MB of memory. I did not load-test this to avoid disturbing the other testers.

findings.title: Failed or cancelled user turns stay in history and get silently merged into the next prompt (one deterministic failure poisons the conversation)
findings.steps: 1) In a conversation, send a message that fails (bad key, provider 500, empty or safety-blocked reply) or press Stop before the first token. 2) Send another message, for example 'keyin', in the same conversation. 3) Inspect /_log on the fake upstream.
findings.expected: A failed or cancelled prompt is not resent, or the user can retry or remove it explicitly. The next question is sent alone.
findings.actual:
The unanswered user message stays in the DB, and merge_history joins consecutive user messages. The provider receives 'salom bad...

keyin...' (the reply shows both). After a Stop before the first token, upstream gets 'bekor qilingan savol

yangi savol'. If the original failure is deterministic (Gemini safety block -> 'Model bo'sh javob qaytardi', a provider 400), every later message in that conversation fails again. In the API run, one xato500 made the next 6 prompts fail, and each had all earlier failed prompts concatenated. The UI gives no hint, and the typed text is not restored for stream errors.

findings.title: Double-clicking Send in an existing conversation cancels the request: the reply never appears and no error is shown
findings.steps: 1) Open a conversation that already has messages (Deepseek Chat). 2) Type a message and double-click the Send button.
findings.expected: One message is sent and its reply streams in, as with a single click.
findings.actual: The first click sets streaming=true, so the Stop button renders in the same spot and the second click calls chat.stop(). The fetch is aborted (net::ERR_ABORTED). The UI shows the user bubble with no reply and no error. The server still stored a full assistant reply, which only appears after reopening the conversation. All scripts, outputs and screenshots are in /tmp/pwrun/ft_chat/ (api_test*.py, models.mjs, multiturn.mjs, stop.mjs, errors.mjs [dark/light], inputs.mjs, dbl.mjs, sidebar.mjs, del2tab.mjs, personalize.mjs, quota.mjs, misc.mjs, viewport.mjs, offline.mjs, toolong.mjs, light.mjs, fly.mjs, earlystop.py, del_during.py; *.out holds the results). No repo files were modified. The shared infrastructure was not touched and /_reset was never called. Keys contained 'chat' plus a random tag, and log entries were filtered by them.
Harness-related caveats:
(1) The fake's 'xato500' is deterministic, so the follow-up failure in the same conversation is amplified by the fake. The merge itself is real: non-error cases ('salom bad\n\nkeyin', and Stop before first token -> 'bekor qilingan savol\n\nyangi savol') show it in the upstream log.

(4) The Anthropic SDK retries 429/500 twice (3 upstream calls, about 1.4s). This is SDK default, not a bug.
(5) Chromium setOffline did not cut an in-flight localhost SSE stream, so the mid-stream network-drop UI was observed via the delete-during-stream case instead.
(6) Deepseek reasoner reasoning_content, Gemini thinking and real safety blocks are not emulated by the fake. Nothing was tested with real API keys.
Out of my area but seen in the shared backend.log: concurrent registration with the same email (auth-race2-*) raises an unhandled UniqueViolation -> HTTP 500 instead of 409. Worth cross-checking with the auth tester.

findings.expected: At most 3 succeed; the user ends with 20 providers.
findings.actual: All 12 returned 201; the user has 29 providers. Sequential adds are blocked correctly at 20.
findings.evidence: /tmp/pwrun/ft_models/t5b_race.py output: '[201 x12] final count 29'
findings.suspected_location: backend/app/routers/providers.py:72-75. The count is checked, then the DB session is closed and the model list is fetched over the network (await) before the insert. There is no lock or constraint, so parallel requests all pass the check. Re-count inside a locked transaction (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the user row) right before the insert.

findings.title: SSRF guard allows the 100.64.0.0/10 range (includes Alibaba Cloud metadata 100.100.100.200)
findings.steps: With the production default ALLOW_LOCAL_PROVIDERS=false, run netguard.check_url('http://100.64.0.1/v1') (offline, separate process), or add a custom provider with base URL http://100.100.100.200/... .
findings.expected: Rejected as an internal address.
findings.actual: check_url returns the URL unchanged (allowed). Loopback, RFC1918, link-local, IPv6-mapped, decimal-IP and 0.0.0.0 are blocked correctly. Python reports is_private=False and is_global=False for 100.64/10, so the denylist misses it.
findings.evidence: Offline probe output: 'http://100.64.0.1/v1 -> ALLOWED'; ipaddress flags: '100.100.100.200 private False reserved False global False'
findings.suspected_location: backend/app/netguard.py:32. Use `not ip.is_global` (or add 100.64.0.0/10). Also, the URL is only checked on add/refresh; catalog.resolve (backend/app/catalog.py:82) and chat/agent calls do not re-check it. That leaves a DNS-rebinding window, which I did not test.

reports.harness_notes:
Everything is under /tmp/pwrun/ft_models/: API tests t1–t11 (*.py, run with the backend venv python -I), browser tests u1–u11 (*.mjs) with their PNG screenshots, and lib.py / h.mjs helpers. I changed no repo files and did not reset the shared fake log (filtered by my own keys and text tags).

Things the fake harness caused, not product bugs:
1) After an 'xato500' message fails, the next message in the same conversation also gets a 500. The failed user turn is merged into the next one (merge_history, intended), and the fake matches 'xato500' in the merged text. I used fresh conversations for error tests.
2) The fake /responses log has no has_image field. Codex image input was checked by the reply text and code reading (_responses_input sends input_image).
3) Every request to the whisper model 'works' in the fake. The real Groq API would reject chat/completions for it.
4) The 200-item picker cap, the long AI-tab list and the long-model-id UI case were tested by adding models to /api/models with Playwright page.route. The fake lists only a few models. The long-id data loss itself was confirmed end to end against the real backend and database (t10b_longid.py).
5) This environment runs with ALLOW_LOCAL_PROVIDERS=true. I tested the SSRF guard offline by importing app.netguard in a separate process with the default false. DNS rebinding and re-checking the URL at chat time were not exercised.

Not tested: real provider API keys, real Groq/Mistral/Together/xAI model lists (whether embedding/TTS models would leak is from reading code), real OpenAI reasoning-token budgets (max_output_tokens=8192 for codex may truncate in reality).

Server error messages are Uzbek-only in EN/RU (e.g. bad-key toast 'API kalit noto'g'ri...'). This is already on the roadmap, so I did not file it separately.

Side effect: I created many test accounts (models-*@example.com) and providers in the shared database.

reports.harness_notes:
Hech bir repo faylini o'zgartirmadim; barcha skriptlar va skrinshotlar /tmp/pwrun/ft_canvas/ da (t1_preview … t14_double_send .mjs, *.png). Umumiy servislarni to'xtatmadim, /_reset chaqirmadim; /_log ni o'z kalitlarim bo'yicha filtrladim (sk-good-canvas*-…, platform-gemini-ok + 'canvas' matni).
Harness bilan bog'liq, product bug EMAS: (1) Excalidraw shriftlarining yuklanmasligi (ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED) — sandboxda internet yo'q; product kamchiligi faqat CDN ga bog'liqlikning o'zi. (2) Gemini /_log dagi 'user' oldidagi bo'sh joy — soxta server rasm qismi matnini ' ' bilan qo'shadi. (3) Soxta server 'html' so'zi bor har qanday matnga HTML javob beradi (masalan data:text/html havolasi testida) — testni boshqa matn bilan takrorladim. (4) Preview chekka holatlarini tekshirish uchun custom_instructions + 'SYSTEMCHECK' (soxta model system promptni qaytaradi) orqali javobga kod bloklarini kiritdim; '```>>' qoldig'i soxta server formatidan. (5) Canvasga rasm qo'yish sintetik drop hodisasi bilan qilindi (Chromium'da showOpenFilePicker ni Playwright ushlay olmaydi). (6) Sidebar'dagi takror suhbatlar (canvas-2, canvas-13) — skriptlarimni qayta ishga tushirganim natijasi, t14 dagisidan tashqari.
Haqiqiy API kalitlarisiz: Claude/Gemini haqiqatda rasmni (canvas) tushunishi va haqiqiy Gemini rasm modeli javobi sinalmagan — faqat simli format (has_image, inlineData) tekshirildi. Soxta rasmlar 64x64 (179 bayt), shuning uchun galereyaning haqiqiy hajmli rasmlar bilan tezligi (60 ta to'liq o'lchamli rasm, thumbnail/lazy-loading yo'q) o'lchanmadi. Cheksiz sikl testi faqat Chromium'da (sandbox iframe alohida jarayonda) — Firefox'da sahifa qotishi mumkin, sinalmadi. '```svg' bloklari preview qilinmaydi (faqat html/css/js qo'llab-quvvatlanadi) — dizayn bo'yicha, bug sifatida yozilmadi. Media Studio'da generatsiya paytida sahifadan ketib qaytishni sinab bo'lmadi: soxta Gemini 0.3s da javob beradi. Platforma limiti testi uchun canvas-9 akkauntida 25 ta so'rov ishlatildi (oylik limit tugagan).

reports.harness_notes:
Shared services were restarted around 09:02 (backend, frontend and fake logs were empty). Everything was healthy afterwards and I did not restart or kill anything. I edited no files in the repo; all scripts and screenshots are in /tmp/pwrun/ft_settings/ (responsive shots in /tmp/pwrun/ft_settings/resp/).

1. Double-click key save: in this harness the frontend (:3000) and backend (:8000) are on different origins. A FastAPI 500 then comes back without CORS headers, so the toast reads 'Backend bilan aloqa yo‘q...' instead of 'Server xatosi (500)'. Under Caddy (same origin) the text would differ, but the 500 is a real backend race; I reproduced it with plain Python requests (race.py).
2. Uzbek dates 'M10 10': this comes from the Chromium build's trimmed ICU data (HeadlessChrome 141). Firefox or a full-ICU browser may show proper Uzbek month names. I report it because Chrome is the main target browser.
3. The fake upstream returns only 3–4 models per custom provider, so I could not test how the AI tab behaves with 300+ OpenRouter models (it renders every model as a button, with no search).
4. Not tested with real API keys; provider behaviour comes from the fake upstream.
5. Accounts used settings-<tag>-<id>@example.com. API keys contained 'settings' (e.g. sk-good-settings-anthropic-ABCD, sk-good-settings-dbl-deepseek-N, sk-good-settings-openrouter-aim).
6. Earlier 'OVERFLOW' checks at 1400px found no clipped text in en/ru; all layout problems are at 375 and 768 widths.

reports.harness_notes: This session continued an earlier run that hit a usage limit; every test script was re-run here and all outputs are fresh (/tmp/pwrun/ft_voice/*.out, *.png). Scripts: api_voice.py, api_quota.py, api_whisper.py, api_extra.py (run with backend/.venv python, shared helpers in api_voice_lib.py); voice_chat.mjs, voice_stale.mjs, voice_wave*.mjs, voice_denied*.mjs, voice_more.mjs, voice_agent.mjs, voice_long.mjs, voice_toggle.mjs, quota_ui.mjs, usage_whisper.mjs (shared helpers in common.mjs). Harness issues, not product bugs: (1) The fake upstream's /oai/{vendor}/audio/transcriptions returns 500 Internal Server Error for any multipart request; it most likely lacks python-multipart, which req.form() needs. The 502 'Provayder serverida xato (500)' in api_quota.out section 5 comes from this. I checked the Whisper path against my own stub instead (/tmp/pwrun/ft_voice/whisper_stub.py on 127.0.0.1:9201, added as a groq/openai provider with base_url http://127.0.0.1:9201/v1; works because ALLOW_LOCAL_PROVIDERS=true). The stub logged real multipart (model whisper-large-v3-turbo / whisper-1, file voice.wav, audio/wav, RIFF header). The stub ran as my background task and stops with this session. (2) Headless Chromium without --use-fake-ui-for-media-stream leaves getUserMedia pending forever (no prompt UI), and CDP Browser.setPermission 'denied' did not change that. I tested the denied path with --deny-permission-prompts (NotAllowedError), which shows the real UI behaviour. (3) The agent page needs the Electron bridge; I tested it in the browser with a fake window.omniDesktop injected via addInitScript. (4) The empty-transcript and network-error UI paths were simulated with page.route on /voice/transcribe. Context: the fake Gemini always returns 'Salom bu ovozli xabar' for audio, so transcription accuracy and real Gemini/Whisper behaviour are untested without real keys. Voice transcription uses one free platform request, so a voice message with auto-send costs 2 of the 25 (by design, but worth knowing). Out of my area / already known: server error messages are Uzbek-only (roadmap item), and the frontend NETWORK_ERROR string (frontend/src/lib/api.ts:8) is hardcoded Uzbek and developer-oriented ('Server (uvicorn) ishlayotganini tekshiring'). I created only voice-*@example.com accounts, never called /_reset, and did not touch the shared services or the repo.

reports.harness_notes:
Nothing inside /home/user/UmarIbnHattob was edited; git status is clean. All scripts, outputs and screenshots are in /tmp/pwrun/ft_quality/. Python helpers are run with backend/.venv/bin/python; .mjs files are run with node, with node_modules symlinked to /tmp/pwrun/node_modules.

The fake upstream accepts things the real APIs reject: chat with Whisper models, tools on no-tool models, and any reasoning-item ordering. So the 200s in those cases are harness artifacts. The findings rest on what the backend sends and lists, not on those 200s.

Unproven risks (no real OpenAI access, so not reported as findings):
(a) Reasoning round-trip in _step_responses. Reasoning items are sent back with their rs_ id, but the following message and function_call items lose their msg_/fc_ ids and become an EasyInputMessage and an id-less function_call. Some reports say this can trigger 400 "Item 'rs_…' of type 'reasoning' was provided without its required following item". An empty {'role':'assistant','content':''} item (refusal or empty message) may also be rejected.
(b) computer-use-preview is listed (not filtered) and routed to Responses. It needs the computer tool, and include=['reasoning.encrypted_content'] on a non-reasoning model may be rejected.
(c) -pro models (o3-pro, gpt-5-pro) stream through TIMEOUT read=60s and can be silent for minutes while reasoning, which would cause a timeout. Also max_output_tokens / max_completion_tokens = 8192 counts reasoning tokens, so answers could come back empty with only the truncation note.
(d) Older OpenAI chat models (gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4-turbo) stay in the list but get max_completion_tokens=8192, above their 4096 output cap. OpenAI would likely return 400.
(e) SSRF: check_url runs only on add and refresh. Chat and agent calls to cp.base_url are not re-validated, so DNS rebinding is possible, and 4xx bodies (300 chars) are echoed to the user. Not testable because the shared backend runs with ALLOW_LOCAL_PROVIDERS=true.
(f) Unhandled 500s carry no CORS headers. This only shows in the cross-origin dev setup (localhost:3000 -> :8000, Umar's local setup), where any 500 appears as 'Backend bilan aloqa yo‘q'. In production the same origin is used.

Environment notes:
- The backend venv is Python 3.13. Python 3.14 (Umar's version) was not tested.
- I could not create a scratch database for a from-scratch `alembic upgrade head` (sandbox permission denied). Instead I compared the SQLAlchemy models with the migrated shared schema read-only (no diff) and confirmed a single alembic head equal to the DB revision.
- The frontend server log warns that 'next start' does not work with output: standalone. That is how the harness launches it, not a product bug.
- 5 of the 11 IntegrityError tracebacks in backend.log came from another tester (last4 'DBL1') before my run; the other 6 are my reproduction. The 3 KeyError tracebacks are from my deliberate malformed-payload tests.
- Ruff found only an unused import (adapters.py:11) and an unused variable (chat.py:130), so these are not reported as bugs.
- The settings tab indicator code (useLayoutEffect + ResizeObserver) was correct in every combination I measured.

reports.harness_notes: Hamma skriptlar, chiqishlar va skrinshotlar: /tmp/pwrun/ft_agent/ (browser_agent.mjs, api_loop.mjs, families.mjs, scen_a..f.mjs, quota.mjs, quota2.mjs, lib.mjs va *.out). Repo faylini o'zgartirmadim. Har Electron ishga tushishda alohida --user-data-dir va yangi loyiha papkasi (proj/...) ishlatildi, shunda requestSingleInstanceLock boshqa testerlar bilan to'qnashmaydi. Sekin, noto'g'ri JSON, traversal, parallel, run_command, 40 qadam kabi holatlar uchun 127.0.0.1:9177 da o'zimning OpenAI-mos mock serverimni (agentmock.py) ishga tushirib, uni custom provayder sifatida qo'shdim (ALLOW_LOCAL_PROVIDERS=true). Ish oxirida u to'xtatildi, /etc ga ko'rsatgan symlink ham o'chirildi. Umumiy infratuzilma (uvicorn/next/postgres/9100) to'xtatilmadi, _reset chaqirilmadi. Soxta upstream bilan bog'liq va mahsulot xatosi deb hisoblanmagan narsalar: (1) soxta model ask_expert ni majburiy 'expertise' maydonisiz chaqiradi — 'undefined' yorlig'ini past darajada qayd etdim, chunki haqiqiy modellar ham maydonni tashlab ketishi mumkin. (2) Soxta rasm 179 bayt, shuning uchun '0 KB rasm' yozuvi — xato emas. (3) Konteynerda xdg-open va terminal emulyatori yo'q: 'Ochish'/'Papkada ko'rsatish' hech narsa qilmadi (xato ham yo'q), 'Terminalda ochish' kutilgandek 'Terminal dasturi topilmadi' dedi. (4) Playwright CDP klaviatura hodisalari mahalliy menyu tezkor tugmalariga (Ctrl+Shift+A) yetmaydi; menyu bandlarini bosish orqali tekshirdim. (5) Soxta upstream Anthropic tool_use/tool_result juftligini va Gemini thoughtSignature'ni tekshirmaydi, log'da ham yozmaydi; signature qaytishini faqat kod orqali (raw o'zgarishsiz yuboriladi) tasdiqlash mumkin. (6) Bitta JS vazifasi ichida ikkita sintetik Enter keydown yuborilganda ikkita parallel ishga tushish va umumiy messages.current buzilishi kuzatildi, lekin haqiqiy (alohida) klaviatura hodisalari bilan qaytarilmadi, shuning uchun finding sifatida berilmadi. Haqiqiy Claude API bunday tarixni rad etgan bo'lardi. (7) Boshlanishdagi console 401 — login oldidan /me tekshiruvi, kutilgan. (8) Ruxsat oynalari dialog.showMessageBox'ni almashtirish orqali tekshirildi; haqiqiy mahalliy oyna ko'rinishi (uzun detail'da tugmalar sig'ishi) faqat npm test darajasida tasdiqlangan. Haqiqiy API kalitlari bilan hech narsa sinalmadi.

verdicts.title: Chat page is not responsive: chat column collapses at tablet/phone widths and after shrinking the window (including the desktop app at its own minWidth)
verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/hooks/useResizable.ts:18-21: the preview width is computed once on mount (deps [initial, min]), clamped to a 320px minimum, and never recomputed on window resize. frontend/src/components/ChatView.tsx:347 renders the preview with style={{width}} and shrink-0. ChatView.tsx:126 (conversation list w-56 shrink-0) and Sidebar.tsx:22 (aside w-56 shrink-0) are also fixed. The chat column (ChatView.tsx:156, flex-1 min-w-0 overflow-hidden) is the only element that can shrink, so it absorbs all the lost width. The panel is open by default (ChatView.tsx:74 panelOpen=true) and there are no responsive breakpoints anywhere (no sm:/md:/lg: classes in ChatView, Sidebar or AuthGate).
verdicts.evidence: /tmp/pwrun/ft_chat_verify/viewport.mjs -> viewport.out. Textarea width: 1400=348px, 1280=276px, 1024=122px, 768=18px, 390=18px. Resized 1400->1024 gives 18px (preview stays 470px). At 768 the panel toggle click times out; at 390 the toggle is off-screen (x=548). /tmp/pwrun/ft_chat_verify/vp960.mjs -> vp960.out: Electron minWidth is 960 (desktop/src/main.js:24). A fresh load at 960 gives a 58px textarea, and the default 1440 window resized to 960 gives 18px (preview stays 486px). Screenshots vp_768.png (chat column entirely gone), vp_1024.png, vp_resized_1024.png, vp_1440_to_960.png. Closing the panel restores a 446px textarea at 1024, so a workaround exists only while the toggle is still reachable.
verdicts.proposed_fix: In useResizable, watch the container with a ResizeObserver (or a window resize listener) and clamp width to min(width, containerWidth - CHAT_MIN), where CHAT_MIN is about 360px. Give the chat column min-w-[360px]. Below the lg breakpoint, default panelOpen to false or show the preview as an overlay or tab. Below md, hide the conversation list and nav aside behind a drawer toggle.

verdicts.title: Failed or cancelled user turns stay in history and are silently merged into the next prompt
verdicts.root_cause: backend/app/routers/chat.py:140-150 commits the user Message before streaming. When the stream ends with an error or the client disconnects with no parts, event_stream (chat.py:198-217) saves nothing for the assistant and never removes or flags the user turn. The next request builds its history with merge_history (backend/app/providers/base.py:46-60), which concatenates consecutive user messages with '\n\n'. The merge itself is deliberate: the docstring says a failed reply leaves two adjacent user messages, which Claude rejects. What nobody handled is the consequence: cancelled or failed prompts get re-sent, and there is no retry or remove option. On the frontend, useChat.ts:160-161 (the non-RequestError branch) keeps the user bubble and does not restore the typed text.
verdicts.evidence:
/tmp/pwrun/ft_chat_verify/api_verify.py -> api_verify.out. (a) Bad key, then good key: upstream user = 'birinchi savol 226a86

ikkinchi savol 226a86'. (b) A transient 429, then the next prompt: merged the same way. (d) Client disconnect before the first token: the next upstream prompt is 'bekor qilingan 226a86

yangi savol 226a86', and the DB has two consecutive user rows. UI: /tmp/pwrun/ft_chat_verify/ui3.mjs -> ui3.out failedTurn: after a bad-key failure the bubble stays, the textarea is '' and the banner shows the error. The next send shows two consecutive user bubbles and a reply 'Javob: ilk savol...

ikkinchi savol...' (ui3_failed_turn.png, ui3_failed_turn_next.png). HARNESS NOTE: the claim that 'one xato500 made the next 6 prompts fail' is amplified by the fake upstream, which returns 500 whenever 'xato500' appears anywhere in the merged last user text. I reproduced it (UPSTREAM 'xato500 ..

oddiy savol0 ..

oddiy savol1 ..', all errors), but a real provider 500 is transient. Permanent poisoning in production only follows from content-deterministic failures, such as a Gemini prompt block that returns no candidates and so triggers 'Model bo'sh javob qaytardi' (gemini.py:30-37). I found that path by reading the code; the fake cannot simulate it.
verdicts.proposed_fix: In chat.py, keep the id of the user Message saved at line 141. In event_stream, if no parts were produced (on error or client cancel), delete that message in the finally block, and revert the title if it was just set from it. In useChat.ts, treat a stream error with an empty assistant bubble the same as RequestError: drop both bubbles and setRestoreText(text). Alternatively, add Retry and Delete actions on a failed user bubble, and have merge_history drop unanswered user turns instead of concatenating them.

verdicts.title: Double-clicking Send in an existing conversation aborts the request: no reply is shown and no error appears
verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/hooks/useChat.ts:99 calls setStreaming(true) synchronously. For an existing conversation there is no await before abortRef.current = new AbortController() (useChat.ts:132), so the fetch starts immediately. React re-renders between the two clicks, and ChatView.tsx:322-325 renders the Stop button in the exact spot of Send. The second click calls chat.stop() (useChat.ts:177), which aborts the live controller. The AbortError is swallowed silently (useChat.ts:153). In a new conversation the abort hits a stale controller during the createConversation await, so that case works.
verdicts.evidence: /tmp/pwrun/ft_chat_verify/dbl.mjs -> dbl.out. dblclick: posts=1, failed=['net::ERR_ABORTED'], the UI shows only the user bubble, no banner, and the server has 'user:dblclick egzr3u' with no assistant reply (aborted before the first token). Two clicks 120ms apart: also aborted, and only a truncated 'Javob: dblc' was stored. Screenshot dbl_dblclick.png. Control: a single click works (singleClick posts=1, reply shown). /tmp/pwrun/ft_chat_verify/dbl_new.mjs -> dbl_new.out: a double-click in a new conversation works, matching the report.
verdicts.proposed_fix: In useChat, record sentAt = Date.now() in send, and make stop() a no-op when Date.now() - sentAt < 500ms. Alternatively, render the Stop button disabled for the first ~400ms, or ignore clicks with e.detail > 1 on Stop.

verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/components/ChatView.tsx:144-147: the trash button uses className 'hidden ... group-hover:block' (display:none unless hovered, so it is removed from the tab order), and onClick calls chat.remove(c.id) directly. useChat.ts:81-92 remove() calls DELETE immediately, with no confirm or undo.

verdicts.title: Deleting a conversation while its reply streams crashes the stream (FK violation), shows raw 'network error', and leaves the UI on the deleted conversation
verdicts.root_cause: backend/app/routers/chat.py:160-168 save_reply inserts the assistant Message for conv_uuid without checking that the conversation still exists, which raises ForeignKeyViolation. The call at chat.py:207 sits outside the inner try, so the exception propagates. The finally block (chat.py:213-217) retries save_reply and fails again (logged), and the ASGI app errors before the final SSE event, which cuts the chunked body. On the frontend, chatApi.ts:46 reader.read() rejects with Chromium's TypeError 'network error', which useChat.ts:160-161 shows verbatim. activeId still points to the deleted conversation, so the next send gets 404 'Suhbat topilmadi' (no reset on 404).
verdicts.evidence: /tmp/pwrun/ft_chat_verify/del_during.py -> del_during.out: for both a single DELETE and DELETE /conversations (delete all), the result is RemoteProtocolError 'incomplete chunked read' with no done or error event. del_during_backend.log shows psycopg ForeignKeyViolation at chat.py:207 -> save_reply chat.py:167, again at chat.py:215, then 'Exception in ASGI application'. UI: /tmp/pwrun/ft_chat_verify/ui3.mjs -> ui3.out deleteDuring: banner ['network error'], sidebar empty while the deleted chat is still shown, and the next send gives banner ['Suhbat topilmadi'] (text restored). Screenshots ui3_delete_during.png, ui3_delete_during_next.png.
verdicts.proposed_fix: In save_reply, do c = s.get(Conversation, conv_uuid) first, and if c is None return None without inserting. Wrap chat.py:207 in try/except so a final SSE event (error 'Suhbat o‘chirildi' or done) is always sent. In useChat, on a RequestError with 404 for the active conversation, call select(null) and refreshConversations(). In chatApi.ts, catch reader errors and throw a localized 'connection lost' message.

verdicts.title: Sending while offline: the bubble stays as if sent, the typed text is cleared (lost entirely in a new chat), and the error text is developer-oriented
verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/lib/api.ts:15-18 turns a fetch failure into a plain Error(NETWORK_ERROR), not a RequestError. useChat.ts:152-162 restores text and removes the bubbles only for RequestError (lines 155-159), so a network failure leaves the optimistic bubble and never restores the text. In a new chat, createConversation (useChat.ts:123) fails before the bubbles are added, so the text is simply gone. verdicts.title: Platform free quota is consumed by requests that fail upstream
verdicts.root_cause: backend/app/quota.py:64 calls _consume() (quota.py:30-41, an atomic increment) inside resolve_key. That runs from resolve() at chat.py:133 before streaming starts, and event_stream (chat.py:187-217) never refunds when the provider errors or returns nothing.
verdicts.evidence: /tmp/pwrun/ft_chat_verify/api_verify.py (quota section) -> api_verify.out: usage before used=0. After 'xato500 q' on Gemini 2.5 Flash with the platform key (error 'Provayder serverida xato (500)'), used=1. After a successful send, used=2.

verdicts.title: After logout, browser Back shows the previous user's settings page from the HTTP cache (no Cache-Control on API responses)
verdicts.root_cause: backend/app/main.py:8-28: nothing sets Cache-Control on /api responses. Measured on /me, /auth/me, /conversations, /me/export, /keys and /usage/stats: no Cache-Control, ETag, Last-Modified or Expires header. So Chromium stores GET /api/me in its disk cache. On a back/forward document load, Blink serves default-mode subresource fetches from the cache even when stale. frontend/src/lib/me.ts:32 fetchMe() uses the default cache mode, so after logout it gets the old 200 from cache. AuthGate.tsx:53-55 then sets `me` to the previous user. Settings tabs that make no other API call (General, Account, Privacy, Shortcuts, Desktop) keep showing the old data. Tabs or pages that make another call (AI tab /models, /media, /chat /models) get a 401 and redirect to /login.
verdicts.evidence:
Script: /tmp/pwrun/ft_auth_verify/v1_cache.mjs, output in v1_cache.out and v1_cache_BC.out. Three scenarios: (A) the reported steps; (B) UI login > Settings from the sidebar > F5 > logout > Back twice; (C) the same as A, but Playwright adds 'Cache-Control: no-store' to every /api response to test the fix.
- A, tab=account: url=/settings?tab=account, name and email of the old user visible, cookies=0, 'afterBack 200 /me disk=true'. The page was still on /settings 5 s later. Screenshot: /tmp/pwrun/ft_auth_verify/v1_A_account.png.
- A, tab=ai: '200 /me disk=true', then '401 /models', then redirect to /login.
- B: the first Back is a same-document SPA entry and redirects correctly. The second Back gives '200 /me disk=true' and then a 401 on /models, so the chat page shows only briefly.
- C (no-store): 'afterBack 401 /me disk=false', redirect to /login.
- API headers: /tmp/pwrun/ft_auth_verify/api_verify.out shows 'Cache-Control: None' on every authenticated GET.
Scope of the leak: only the /me fields (email, display name, nickname, registration date, avatar). No conversations, keys or custom instructions, because the AI tab redirects. The stale page cannot do anything, since every action gets a 401. Medium because it is real PII exposure on shared computers after an explicit logout. The plain sidebar flow (B) only shows a short flash, which argues for low-medium.
verdicts.proposed_fix:
In backend/app/main.py, after the CORS middleware is added:
```python
@app.middleware("http")
async def no_store(request, call_next):
    resp = await call_next(request)
    resp.headers.setdefault("Cache-Control", "no-store")
    return resp
```
I checked this fix with header injection (scenario C) and it works. Optionally also pass `cache: "no-store"` in fetchMe (me.ts:32), authApi.fetchMe and request() (api.ts:15).

verdicts.title: Canvas drawing in localStorage carries over to the next account on the same browser
verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/components/CanvasPanel.tsx:8 uses a global `STORAGE_KEY = "omniai-canvas-v1"`. It is read in loadSaved() (line 15), passed as initialData (line 65) and written on every change (line 72). The key has no user scope. AuthGate.tsx:94-100 logout() only calls the API and runs setMe(null). It never clears per-user localStorage, and neither does account deletion. ChatView.tsx:108-117 exports this shared scene as a PNG when 'Canvasni AI ga ko‘rsatish' is ticked. useChat.ts and agent/page.tsx keep a global MODEL_KEY in the same way, which leaks less but has the same pattern.
verdicts.evidence:
Script: /tmp/pwrun/ft_auth_verify/v2_canvas.mjs, output in v2_canvas.out. Steps: user1 registers in the UI, opens Chat > Canvas and types 'USER1 SECRET NOTE'. Results:
- 'user1 saved canvas bytes: 639 contains text: true'
- After logout: 'localStorage keys after logout: ["omniai-font","omniai-lang","omniai-canvas-v1","omniai-theme"] canvas bytes: 639'

verdicts.proposed_fix: Scope the key per user. Also delete the legacy unscoped key once with `localStorage.removeItem("omniai-canvas-v1")`. As defense in depth, in AuthGate.logout() and after account deletion remove the user-scoped keys, e.g. `Object.keys(localStorage).filter(k => k.startsWith("omniai-canvas") || k.endsWith("-model")).forEach(k => localStorage.removeItem(k))` inside try/catch.

verdicts.title: Logout does not invalidate the session token on the server (JWT valid for 7 more days)
verdicts.root_cause: backend/app/routers/auth.py:80-82: logout() only calls response.delete_cookie. Sessions are stateless HS256 JWTs carrying {sub, tv, exp} (security.py:43-46), and revocation is per user through token_version (deps.py:26-27). That is the mechanism CLAUDE.md decision #3 records: 'JWT, token_version bilan bekor qilinadi'. With no per-session state, the server cannot revoke one device's token. The product offers 'Barcha qurilmalardan chiqish' for that (me.py:88-90, hint 'Bu qurilma ham, boshqalari ham hisobdan chiqadi'). So the behavior is real, but it is the documented trade-off of the chosen design.
verdicts.evidence:
/tmp/pwrun/ft_auth_verify/api_verify.py, output in api_verify.out:
- 'logout 204 set-cookie: omniai_session=""; ... Max-Age=0'
- 'reuse /auth/me with old token: 200 {...}'
- 'reuse /me with old token: 200'
logout-all does revoke: in v3_misc.out (export section), after another client calls /me/logout-all, the first session gets 401. Exploiting this needs a stolen httpOnly cookie.
verdicts.proposed_fix: Optional hardening if per-device logout must be server-side: add a `jti` claim and a small `revoked_tokens(jti, exp)` table, or a `sessions` table, checked in get_current_user; on logout insert the jti. A cheaper alternative is to shorten session_days. Bumping token_version on plain logout would also log out every other device, which changes the UX on purpose.

verdicts.title: Two simultaneous registrations with the same email: losers get a 500 without CORS headers, and the UI says 'backend not reachable'
verdicts.root_cause: backend/app/routers/auth.py:47-58 does check-then-insert with no IntegrityError handling. The SELECT at :47 runs, then hash_password (scrypt N=2^15, tens of ms) at :56 widens the window, then db.commit() at :58 raises psycopg UniqueViolation on users_email_key. The uncaught exception is turned into a 500 by Starlette's ServerErrorMiddleware, which sits outside CORSMiddleware, so the response has no Access-Control-Allow-Origin. The browser fetch then fails as a network error, and api.ts:16-18 shows NETWORK_ERROR. From code reading only (not reproducible without resetting the shared DB): the legacy-claim branch (:51-54) is also racy. Two concurrent first registrations can both UPDATE the legacy row, and the second overwrites email and password_hash while the first client's cookie (same id, same token_version) stays valid.
verdicts.evidence:
API, /tmp/pwrun/ft_auth_verify/api_verify.out: 4 concurrent POST /api/auth/register with the same email, 3 trials. Every trial gives exactly one (201, 'http://localhost:3000') and three (500, None, 'Internal Server Error'). Sequential duplicates give 201 then 409 'Bu email allaqachon ro'yxatdan o'tgan.' with CORS.
UI, /tmp/pwrun/ft_auth_verify/v3_misc.mjs race section, output in v3_misc.out: 3 browser contexts submit at once.
- tab0: 'Backend bilan aloqa yo‘q. Server (uvicorn) ishlayotganini tekshiring.' (screenshot v3_race_tab0.png)
- tab1: /chat
- tab2: the correct 409 text.
The fulltest backend.log contains 'psycopg.errors.UniqueViolation: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_email_key"'.

verdicts.proposed_fix:
In register():
```python
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
...
try:
    db.commit()
except IntegrityError:
    db.rollback()
    raise HTTPException(409, "Bu email allaqachon ro'yxatdan o'tgan.")
```
For the legacy branch, use `select(User).where(User.email == LEGACY_EMAIL).with_for_update()` (or a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE password_hash IS NULL` and check rowcount). Optionally add a global exception handler that returns JSON errors with CORS headers, so unexpected 500s do not show up as 'backend not reachable'.

verdicts.title: Export link with an expired or revoked session navigates the tab to raw API JSON
verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/components/settings/PrivacyTab.tsx:19 is a plain `<a href={`${API_URL}/me/export`}>`. With a valid cookie the backend sends Content-Disposition, so the browser downloads the file and stays on the page. With a 401 there is no attachment header, so the browser navigates the top-level tab to the JSON error body. The request() 401 handling (auth-expired event) is bypassed.
verdicts.evidence:

- Valid session: 'download= true omniai-export-2026-10-10.json url now: http://localhost:3000/settings?tab=privacy'

"")?.[1] ?? "omniai-export.json" }); a.click(); URL.revokeObjectURL(url);` with try/catch that calls toast(). request() already dispatches auth-expired on a 401, so AuthGate sends the user to /login. The backend must expose the header (`expose_headers=["Content-Disposition"]` in CORSMiddleware) when the origins differ, or the frontend can build the filename itself.

verdicts.title: Assistant reply is lost (stream cut, never saved) when the model id is longer than 60 characters

The finally block (213-217) then tries the same insert again and fails a second time ('Qisman javobni saqlab bo'lmadi' in the backend log). In the frontend the browser's raw 'network error' TypeError reaches useChat.ts setError unchanged.

In chat.py event_stream, wrap the save at line 207 in try/except: log the error, set error='Javobni saqlab bo'lmadi', and still yield an 'error' SSE event so the stream ends cleanly. verdicts.title: Auto classifier misses common Uzbek/Russian code requests (word endings break the regex)
verdicts.root_cause: backend/app/providers/router_auto.py:17-21. Each _CODE alternative ends with \b, so inflected Uzbek and Russian forms do not match: 'kodni', 'funksiyani', 'dasturni', 'функцию', 'ошибку', 'коде', 'сайта'. The stems 'функци' and 'ошибк' can never match, because a letter always follows them (даже 'функция'). _REASON (line 22-24) uses \w*, so 'plan\w*' matches 'planshet'.

The next sequential add correctly returns 400 'Ko'pi bilan 20 ta provayder...'. I lowered the severity: the bypass only affects the user's own catalog and DB storage, it needs a burst while under the limit, and opening more accounts gives the same result.
verdicts.proposed_fix: After the network fetch and before the insert, re-check inside the same transaction under a lock: db.execute(select(User).where(User.id==user_id).with_for_update()), recount, and raise 400 if the count is >= MAX_PROVIDERS. Then insert and commit. Or use pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(user_id)).

verdicts.title: SSRF guard allows the 100.64.0.0/10 range (includes Alibaba Cloud metadata 100.100.100.200)
verdicts.root_cause: backend/app/netguard.py:32 uses a denylist (is_private/is_loopback/is_link_local/is_reserved/is_multicast/is_unspecified). For 100.64.0.0/10 (shared/CGNAT address space) Python returns False for all of these, so check_url allows it. That range includes Alibaba Cloud's metadata service 100.100.100.200 and Tailscale addresses. Also, catalog.resolve (catalog.py:78-88) and the chat/agent calls reuse cp.base_url without calling check_url again, so the check only happens when the provider is added or refreshed. friendly_http_error (providers/base.py:26) returns up to 300 characters of a 4xx response body to the user, so this SSRF is partly readable.
verdicts.evidence: /tmp/pwrun/ft_models_verify/v8_ssrf.py run with ALLOW_LOCAL_PROVIDERS=false (Python 3.13.16, separate process): 'http://100.64.0.1/v1 -> ALLOWED' and 'http://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data -> ALLOWED'. 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, 10.0.0.1, [::ffff:127.0.0.1], 2130706433, 0.0.0.0, 198.18.0.1, [fd00::1], 192.0.0.170 and NAT64 [64:ff9b::7f00:1] are all blocked. ipaddress reports 100.100.100.200 private=False reserved=False global=False. The running shared backend has ALLOW_LOCAL_PROVIDERS=true, so a live test is not meaningful; the offline test calls the same function. I did not test DNS rebinding.
verdicts.proposed_fix: In netguard.py:32, add 'not ip.is_global' to the existing conditions and keep the current checks (NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 reports is_global=True but is_reserved=True, so keeping is_reserved matters). Also check ip.ipv4_mapped when it is set. Call check_url again in catalog.resolve and in the agent path before each request, or pin the resolved IP for the httpx request.

verdicts.title: Once a default model is set, the model picked in chat resets on every reload
verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/hooks/useChat.ts:39-41. The comment says the intended priority order: 'Sozlamalardagi standart model > shu brauzerda oxirgi tanlangan > ro'yxatdagi birinchisi'.
